## Harper's transliteration, line by line (col · line · text)
Raised text in braces: {b}, {ilu} = the divine determinative (write it {d} with the AN sign, role det), {amêlu} = the LÚ determinative, {kam}. Harper writes many logograms as the Akkadian word (eḳlam for A.ŠÀ) — the plate decides the sign. ḳ = q.

## Notes from the transcription (apparatus)

- Col. XXXIV: from §206 through §221 Harper's running line numerals are one higher than the ranges in his own §-headings (text gives the column 96 lines, headings imply 95). The source follows the running numerals; check the column length against the autograph plate before citing by line.
- Col. XXXVIII 31–36: not in Harper — §262 breaks off after line 30 in a row of dots (damage on the stele) and §263 begins at 37.
- XXXV 88: Harper misprints the line numeral as '98'; recorded as 88.
- Harper's printed line numerals from XXXIV 13 onward run one higher than his headings: § 206 heading says 4–12 but text runs 4–13 (line 13 'u A.ZU {b}i-ip-pa-al' sits under § 206); § 207 heading 13–18, text numerals 14–19; § 208 heading 19–21, text 20–22. Transcribed numerals and headings as printed; the offset continues on the following pages.
- Fractions ⅓ (XXXIII 73, XXXIV 21) and ½ (XXXIV 18) printed as stacked fractions; rendered with Unicode ⅓ ½.
- XXXIII 91 and XXXIV 19–22 etc.: 'X', 'I', 'I ŠU.ŠI' are Roman-numeral quantities in the text, kept as printed.
- XXXIV 5 'ri-is-{b}ba-tim' and XXXIV 14 'ma-{b}ḫa-zi-šu' are broken across printed lines / have raised b mid-word; joined as printed.
- Continuing the offset from the previous page: every law's printed text numerals run one higher than its heading range (§ 209 heading 22–29, text 23–30; ... § 217 heading 69–72, text 70–73). Both transcribed exactly as printed. Note XXXIV 22 therefore appears as the last line of § 208 on the previous page while § 209's heading starts at 22.
- XXXIV 54: the š of 'i-ša-ḳal' carries both a caron and a dot below (printed ṣ̌); transcribed as 'i-ṣ̌a-ḳal'. Elsewhere this word is i-ša-ḳal — likely a typo/blemish in Harper; human check. A faint mark over the a of ḳal also, probably a speck.
- XXXIV 27 'uš-ta-dí-ši' has an acute on the i (dí), as printed; contrast 'uš-ta-ad-di-ši' at 38 and 48.
- XXXIV 41 'ši' (no -i) vs 31/51 'ši-i' — as printed.
- XXXIV 25 'im-ḫa-aṣ-ma' and 56 'kab-tam', 63 'a-wi-lim' broken across printed lines; joined.
- XXXIV 60: final m of 'a-wi-lim' slightly malformed in print; read lim.
- Heading/numeral offset in col. XXXIV continues: § 218 heading 73–82, text 74–83; § 219 heading 83–87, text 84–88; § 220 heading 88–93, text 89–94; § 221 heading 'XXXIV, 94–XXXV, 9' but text numerals reach XXXIV 96 before XXXV, 1. So Harper's printed numerals give col. XXXIV 96 lines vs. his headings' 95 (and the § 221 heading's 94 start vs. text 95). From XXXV, 1 onward numerals and headings agree again (§ 222 10–12 etc.). All transcribed as printed — human should decide which numbering to trust.
- XXXIV 92 'uḫ-tab-da (=it)' — Harper's parenthetical correction, copied as printed (space before the parenthesis).
- XXXIV 83 'rittê-šu' with circumflex ê; XXXIV 94 'šîmi-šu' with circumflex î.
- XXXIV 84 'zi-ma-am' (single m) as printed, vs. 'zi-im-ma-am' at 75.
- XXXV 20, 24: small marks under the m of 'imêram'/'imêrim' (and under the i of 'i-bu-uš-ma' at XXXV 22) look like broken-type specks, not dots below; transcribed plain m / i. Human check if desired. 'imêrim' at XXXV 19 has no such mark.
- XXXV 21 'ṣi-im-ma-am' with ṣ (dot below), vs. 'ṣi-im-mi-im' at XXXV 6 and 'zi-im-ma-am' in col. XXXIV — as printed.
- XXXIV 90 'sipar-rim' broken across printed lines; joined. XXXV 6 'ṣi-im-mi-im' and 9 'i-na-ad-di-in' broken across lines; joined.
- XXXV 35 'i-na-ad-dí-in' — acute on i (dí) clearly printed; elsewhere i-na-ad-di-in.
- XXXV 31 'i-bu-uš-ma': tiny mark over the u of bu, judged a speck (not an accent).
- XXXV 33 'IGI.IV.GAL' broken across printed lines after 'IGI.IV.'; joined without space. Other line-broken words joined: 40 u-gal-li-ib, 55 u-ta-aš-šar, 71 uš-ta-mi-it.
- XXXV 60 'I SAR' — Roman numeral I quantity + SAR, as printed.
- XXXV 51: speck under the 1 of numeral 51; XXXV 75: speck between a and ti in 'šu-a-ti' — ignored.
- XXXV 88: Harper misprints the line numeral as '98' ('bîtam i-bu-šu 98 la u-dan-ni-nu-ma 89'); recorded as ln 88 since it sits between 87 and 89. The printed numeral is 98.
- PAGE END: the last printed token on the page is the bare numeral '51' (XXXVI 51), with its text on the next page. Line 51 is therefore NOT included here; the next page's carry should begin at XXXVI 51 (§ 237 continues, heading range 38–55).
- XXXVI 30 'ig-rí-im' — acute on the i of rí, as printed.
- XXXVI 7 'šiḳil': a small stroke over the ḳ (like an acute), probably a stray mark; transcribed plain šiḳil.
- XXXVI 41 'šeʾam' — Harper's apostrophe rendered as ʾ (U+02BE).
- XXXVI 5 'LX GUR' quantity as printed.
- XXXVI 29 'mal-aḫim' and 45 'ma-laḫum' broken across printed lines at those hyphens; joined with hyphen kept as instructed (normally malaḫum). Similarly 37 'i-ri-a-ab', 94 'i-bu-uš-ma', XXXVI 3 'u-dan-na-an', 17 'iz-za-par', 22 'ra-ma-ni-šu'.

- XXXVI 76 'ma-ḫi-ir-tim' and 78 'u-te-ib-bu-u': small specks under the final m / final u; treated as specks, not diacritics (no ṃ/ụ).
- XXXVI 84: printed fraction ⅓ (1 over 3).
- XXXVI 88: a small tilde-like mark after 'ŠE.GUR'; treated as a speck.
- Fractions written as ⅓ (lines XXXIII 73, XXXIV 21) and ½ (XXXIV 18); printed as small stacked fractions. Denominator of XXXIII 73 is faint, read as 3.
- XXXIV 3 i-na-ak-ki-su and XXXIV 5 ri-is-{b}ba-tim: plain s clearly printed (no háček) — copied as printed.
- XXXIV 10: "i-na i-du-u" as printed.
- XXXIV 28: "sikil" — no háček visible on the s (faint area); elsewhere šiḳil. Transcribed as visible; verify.
- XXXIV 36: "ma-" / "ḫa-zi-im" broken across printed lines, joined as ma-ḫa-zi-im. XXXIV 56 "kab-"/"tam" joined; XXXIV 63 "a-wi-"/"lim" joined; XXXIV 33 "mâra-"/"zu" joined as mâra-zu.
- XXXIV 41: "ši" (not ši-i) as printed.
- XXXIV 60: read na-gab-ti (g clear on zoom).
- Fractions ½ (XXXIV 43), ⅓ (XXXIV 53) printed as small stacked fractions.
- XXXIV 78 "us-ta-mi-it" and XXXIV 82 "uh-tab-bi-it": no háček on s, no breve under h, no dot under final t visible in the faint print (cf. clearly printed uš-ta-mi-it at XXXIV 87 and uḫ-tab-da at 92). Transcribed as visible; diacritics may have failed to print — human check advised. Same caveat for "i-na-ki-su" (83) and siparrim (plain s, as elsewhere).
- XXXIV 84 "zi-ma-am" (single m) as printed, unlike zi-im-ma-am at 75. XXXV 21 "ṣi-im-ma-am" with ṣ as printed.
- Line-number offset: in col. XXXIV text numerals run one ahead of headings (§ 218 heading 73–82, text 74–83; § 219 83–87 vs 84–88; § 220 88–93 vs 89–94; § 221 starts at 95 vs heading 94). From col. XXXV the text numerals match the headings again.
- XXXIV 92: "(=it)" printed with spaces "( =it )" — transcribed as (=it).
- XXXV 33: "IGI.IV.GAL" split across printed lines as "IGI.IV." / "GAL", joined. Following word reads "simi-su" with no visible háček on either s (cf. šîmi-šu at XXXIV 94 on p. 102) and no visible circumflex on the i. Transcribed as visible; diacritics likely failed to print — verify.
- XXXV 34: "imérim" — vowel mark over e looks like an acute after zoom, but may be a broken circumflex (cf. imêram XXXV 29, imêrim XXXV 19/24). Verify.
- XXXV 75: "bânîm" — mark over the second i is ambiguous between circumflex and acute (bâním); transcribed with circumflex. Verify.

- XXXV 40 u-gal-li-ib, 55 u-ta-aš-šar, 71 {b}uš-ta-mi-it, 81 i-na-ad-di-in: words broken across printed lines, joined.

- XXXV 82: "sum-ma SA.GA" — no háček visible on either s in the faint top line (cf. ŠA.GA clearly at XXXV 90 and XXXVI 22). Transcribed as visible; diacritics likely failed to print — verify.

## Signs already in the shared sign glossary (signs-cuneiform.json) — key: values

- AN: an, diĝir (as det. {d}), Akkadian: Anum (the sky-god, the bare sign), ilum “god”
- NAM: Akkadian: nam
- LUGAL: Akkadian value šarrum “king”
- TA: ta
- E: e, e₃, è, Akkadian: e
- NE: ne, de₃, bil, dè — in A.GA.NE (Agade), bí
- A: Akkadian: a, A.ŠÀ = eqlum “field”, plural marker with ḪI (Harper reads ḪI+A as ZUN, §35)
- BA: Akkadian: ba
- NUN: nun, eridu (with KI), Akkadian: nun
- KI: ki 'place/earth', Akkadian: ki, qi₂; also the syllable ki in words
- LU: Akkadian: lu, second sign of SIPA “shepherd”, as logogram UDU — “sheep”, Akkadian immerum, lū “or; let …”, ṣēnum “sheep,
- LA: Akkadian: la
- GAR: ĝar, gar, qar — in qar-ra-dum “warrior”, GAR/NINDA — “bread, portion”, ŠA.GA (Harper) / NÍG.GA = makkūrum “property” (§6
- MU: Akkadian: mu, MU = šattum “year”: MU III{kam} “the third year” (§30)
- NI: ni, ì, Akkadian: ni, li₂, ì
- AK: ak, aĝ₂, aq
- IB: Akkadian: ib, ip, the god Uraš of Dilbat ({d}IB)
- BI: Akkadian: bi, bé, pi₂
- RU: ru, šub, Akkadian: ru
- DU: du, ĝen, gub, rá, DU — “to go, stand”
- EN: Akkadian: en; EN = bēlum “lord”; EN.LÍL = the god Enlil
- ME: Akkadian: me
- LU2: lù, lú, determinative before persons: {amēlu}agram “hireling” (§26, §33)
- NA: Akkadian: na
- GAL: GAL — “great”; GAL.GAL “the great (gods)”; GAL.BÚR = ušumgallum “dragon”; gál
- TUR: dumu, tur, as DUMU — “son”, Akkadian mārum, DUMU — mār “son”, DUMU+ti = mārtum “daughter” (§38–39)
- ZI: Akkadian: ṣi, ṣe
- PA: pa, sib (PA.LU), Akkadian: pa, PA.LU = SIPA “shepherd” (rēʾûm); PA.AL = šabra (in Mashkan-shabri), PA.PA — the captain (
- RA: Akkadian: ra
